annotation.title_clean: Rethinking the I-You relation through dialogical philosophy in the Ethics of AI and robotics
annotation.title_en: Rethinking the I-You relation through dialogical philosophy in the Ethics of AI and robotics
annotation.summary_en: Editorial introducing an AI & Society special issue applying Martin Buber's I-Thou dialogical philosophy to robotics and AI. It questions whether relational robots and chatbots treat relationships instrumentally, warns of dehumanisation, and previews contributions debating whether I-Thou relations with artificial agents are possible.
key_provisions_or_claims: Dialogical philosophy (Buber) offers an alternative to egocentric, instrumental views of relationships in robotics and AI.
Humans are never tools, even in formal interactions; robotics should not model relations as instrumental.
Contributors disagree on whether I-Thou relations with artificial agents are possible.
Dehumanisation concerns are neglected in current robotics and AI narratives.
Embodied, present dialogue is foundational to human life.
